sanskrit: sarve bhavāmo madhyasthā rājñaś chandānuvartinaḥ chidraṃ bahu prapaśyantaḥ pāṇḍavānāṃ susaṃvṛtāḥ
english: Let us all remain neutral, acting in accordance with the king's wishes, carefully watching for many weaknesses in the Pāṇḍavas while keeping ourselves well concealed.

sanskrit: duḥśāsana uvāca evam etan mahāprājña yathā vadasi mātula nityaṃ hi me kathayatas tava buddhir hi rocate
english: Duḥśāsana said: It is exactly so, O greatly wise one, just as you say, uncle. Indeed, whenever you speak, your counsel always pleases me.

sanskrit: karṇa uvāca kāmam īkṣāmahe sarve duryodhana tavepsitam aikamatyaṃ hi no rājan sarveṣām eva lakṣyate
english: Karṇa said: We all look upon whatever you desire, Duryodhana, as desirable. Indeed, O king, unanimity of purpose is evident among all of us.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca evam uktas tu karṇena rājā duryodhanas tadā nātihṛṣṭamanāḥ kṣipram abhavat sa parāṅmukhaḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Thus addressed by Karṇa, King Duryodhana at that moment became not very joyful in mind and quickly turned away.

sanskrit: upalabhya tataḥ karṇo vivṛtya nayane śubhe roṣād duḥśāsanaṃ caiva saubaleyaṃ ca tāv ubhau
english: Then Karṇa, perceiving this, opened wide his bright eyes and in anger addressed both Duḥśāsana and the son of Subala together.

sanskrit: uvāca paramakruddha udyamyātmānam ātmanā aho mama mataṃ yat tan nibodhata narādhipāḥ
english: He spoke in utmost fury, rousing himself with his own resolve: "Ah, hear my opinion, O lords of men!"

sanskrit: priyaṃ sarve cikīrṣāmo rājñaḥ kiṃkarapāṇayaḥ na cāsya śaknumaḥ sarve priye sthātum atandritāḥ
english: "We all wish to do what is pleasing to the king, standing with joined hands as his servants, yet we are all unable to remain steadfastly in his service without lapses."

sanskrit: vayaṃ tu śastrāṇy ādāya rathān āsthāya daṃśitāḥ gacchāmaḥ sahitā hantuṃ pāṇḍavān vanagocarān
english: "But let us take up our weapons, mount our chariots, clad in armour, and go together to slay the Pāṇḍavas who roam in the forest."

sanskrit: teṣu sarveṣu śānteṣu gateṣv aviditāṃ gatim nirvivādā bhaviṣyanti dhārtarāṣṭrās tathā vayam
english: "When all of them have been destroyed and have departed to an unknown destination, the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra and we alike shall live without dispute."

sanskrit: yāvad eva paridyūnā yāvac chokaparāyaṇāḥ yāvan mitravihīnāś ca tāvac chakyā mataṃ mama
english: "While they are still impoverished, while they are still overwhelmed by grief, while they are still without allies — that is the time they can be overcome; such is my opinion."

sanskrit: tasya tad vacanaṃ śrutvā pūjayantaḥ punaḥ punaḥ bāḍham ity eva te sarve pratyūcuḥ sūtajaṃ tadā
english: Having heard that speech of his, they all applauded it again and again and replied to the son of a charioteer with "Very well! So be it!"

sanskrit: evam uktvā tu saṃkruddhā rathaiḥ sarve pṛthak pṛthak niryayuḥ pāṇḍavān hantuṃ saṃghaśaḥ kṛtaniścayāḥ
english: Having thus spoken, all of them, filled with rage, set out each in his own chariot, resolved in purpose as a band, to slay the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: tān prasthitān parijñāya kṛṣṇadvaipāyanas tadā ājagāma viśuddhātmā dṛṣṭvā divyena cakṣuṣā
english: Knowing them to be setting out, Kṛṣṇa Dvaipāyana then came, that pure-souled one, perceiving them with his divine eye.

sanskrit: pratiṣidhyātha tān sarvān bhagavāṃl lokapūjitaḥ prajñācakṣuṣam āsīnam uvācābhyetya satvaraḥ
english: And stopping all of them, the Blessed One worshipped by the world went quickly and spoke to him who sat with wisdom as his eye.

sanskrit: vyāsa uvāca dhṛtarāṣṭra mahāprājña nibodha vacanaṃ mama vakṣyāmi tvā kauravāṇāṃ sarveṣāṃ hitam uttamam
english: Vyāsa said: O Dhṛtarāṣṭra, greatly wise one, hear my words. I shall speak to you of the highest good for all the Kauravas.

sanskrit: na me priyaṃ mahābāho yad gatāḥ pāṇḍavā vanam nikṛtyā nirjitāś caiva duryodhanavaśānugaiḥ
english: It does not please me, O mighty-armed one, that the Pāṇḍavas have gone to the forest, defeated by fraud by those who follow in Duryodhana's power.

sanskrit: te smarantaḥ parikleśān varṣe pūrṇe trayodaśe vimokṣyanti viṣaṃ kruddhāḥ karaveyeṣu bhārata
english: Remembering their hardships, O Bhārata, when the thirteenth year is complete, they will release their venom in fury upon the Kauravas.

sanskrit: tad ayaṃ kiṃ nu pāpātmā tava putraḥ sumandadhīḥ pāṇḍavān nityasaṃkruddho rājyahetor jighāṃsati
english: So why does this evil-souled son of yours, so utterly dull of wit, always enraged, seek to slay the Pāṇḍavas for the sake of the kingdom?

sanskrit: vāryatāṃ sādhv ayaṃ mūḍhaḥ śamaṃ gacchatu te sutaḥ vanasthāṃs tān ayaṃ hantum icchan prāṇair vimokṣyate
english: Let this fool be restrained properly; let your son find peace. Wishing to slay those dwelling in the forest, he will forfeit his own life.

sanskrit: yathāha viduraḥ prājño yathā bhīṣmo yathā vayam yathā kṛpaś ca droṇaś ca tathā sādhu vidhīyatām
english: As the wise Vidura says, as Bhīṣma says, as we say, as Kṛpa and Droṇa say — let what is proper be done accordingly.

sanskrit: vigraho hi mahāprājña svajanena vigarhitaḥ adharmyam ayaśasyaṃ ca mā rājan pratipadyathāḥ
english: For conflict with one's own kin is censured by good people, O greatly wise one; it is contrary to dharma and brings dishonour. Do not choose such a path, O king.

sanskrit: samīkṣā yādṛśī hy asya pāṇḍavān prati bhārata upekṣyamāṇā sā rājan mahāntam anayaṃ spṛśet
english: For whatever disregard he shows towards the Pāṇḍavas, O Bhārata — that indifference, O king, will touch upon a great calamity.

sanskrit: atha vāyaṃ sumandātmā vanaṃ gacchatu te sutaḥ pāṇḍavaiḥ sahito rājann eka evāsahāyavān
english: Or else let this dull-spirited son of yours go to the forest together with the Pāṇḍavas, O king, alone and without allies.

sanskrit: tataḥ saṃsargajaḥ snehaḥ putrasya tava pāṇḍavaiḥ yadi syāt kṛtakāryo 'dya bhaves tvaṃ manujeśvara
english: If then affection born of association should arise in your son towards the Pāṇḍavas, you would today have your purpose accomplished, O lord of men.

sanskrit: atha vā jāyamānasya yac chīlam anujāyate śrūyate tan mahārāja nāmṛtasyāpasarpati
english: Or else whatever character arises from one's very birth — that, it is said, O great king, does not depart even with one's very life.

sanskrit: kathaṃ vā manyate bhīṣmo droṇo vā viduro 'pi vā bhavān vātra kṣamaṃ kāryaṃ purā cārtho 'tivartate
english: What indeed does Bhīṣma think, or Droṇa, or Vidura, or yourself? What is the proper course of action here, before the matter goes too far?

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca bhagavan nāham apy etad rocaye dyūtasaṃstavam manye tad vidhinākramya kārito 'smīti vai mune
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: O Blessed One, I too did not approve of praise for the dice-game. I believe that fate, overcoming my will, made me cause it, O sage.

sanskrit: naitad rocayate bhīṣmo na droṇo viduro na ca gāndhārī necchati dyūtaṃ tac ca mohāt pravartitam
english: Neither does Bhīṣma approve of it, nor Droṇa, nor Vidura, nor does Gāndhārī desire the dice-game. And yet it was set in motion out of delusion.

sanskrit: parityaktuṃ na śaknomi duryodhanam acetanam putrasnehena bhagavañ jānann api yatavrata
english: I am unable to abandon Duryodhana, that one devoid of wisdom, O Blessed One of disciplined vows, even though I know it — because of my love for my son.

sanskrit: vyāsa uvāca vaicitravīrya nṛpate satyam āha yathā bhavān dṛḍhaṃ vedmi paraṃ putraṃ paraṃ putrān na vidyate
english: Vyāsa said: O king, son of Vicitravīrya, what you say is true. I know firmly: there is nothing higher than a son, nothing higher than one's children.

sanskrit: indro 'py aśrunipātena surabhyā pratibodhitaḥ anyaiḥ samṛddhair apy arthair na sutād vidyate param
english: Even Indra was awakened by the falling tears of Surabhī. With all other abundant blessings, there is nothing higher than one's own child.

sanskrit: atra te vartayiṣyāmi mahad ākhyānam uttamam surabhyāś caiva saṃvādam indrasya ca viśāṃ pate
english: On this matter I shall narrate to you a great and excellent tale — the conversation between Surabhī and Indra, O lord of men.

sanskrit: triviṣṭapagatā rājan surabhiḥ prārudat kila gavāṃ māta purā tāta tām indro 'nvakṛpāyata
english: Surabhī, the mother of cows, having gone to heaven, wept there long ago, O king, O dear one, and Indra felt compassion for her.

sanskrit: indra uvāca kim idaṃ rodiṣi śubhe kaccit kṣemaṃ divaukasām mānuṣeṣv atha vā goṣu naitad alpaṃ bhaviṣyati
english: Indra said: Why do you weep, O auspicious one? Is all well with the dwellers of heaven, or with humans, or with the cows? This must not be something small.

sanskrit: surabhir uvāca vinipāto na vaḥ kaś cid dṛśyate tridaśādhipa ahaṃ tu putraṃ śocāmi tena rodimi kauśika
english: Surabhī said: No misfortune of yours is to be seen, O lord of the thirty gods. But I grieve for my son — for that reason I weep, O Kauśika.

sanskrit: paśyainaṃ karṣakaṃ raudraṃ durbalaṃ mama putrakam pratodenābhinighnantaṃ lāṅgalena nipīḍitam
english: "Look at this dreadful ploughman striking my weak little son with his goad, tormenting him with the plough."

sanskrit: etaṃ dṛṣṭvā bhṛśaṃ śrantaṃ vadhyamānaṃ surādhipa kṛpāviṣṭāsmi devendra manaś codvijate mama
english: "Seeing him thus utterly exhausted and being beaten, O king of the gods, O lord of Devas, I am seized by pity, and my heart trembles."

sanskrit: ekas tatra balopeto dhuram udvahate 'dhikām aparo 'lpabalaprāṇaḥ kṛśo dhamanisaṃtataḥ kṛcchrād udvahate bhāraṃ taṃ vai śocāmi vāsava
english: "One of them, endowed with strength, draws the yoke-load abundantly; the other, of little strength and vitality, lean and with veins standing out, with great difficulty draws that burden — him indeed I mourn, O Vāsava."

sanskrit: vadhyamānaḥ pratodena tudyamānaḥ punaḥ punaḥ naiva śaknoti taṃ bhāram udvoḍhuṃ paśya vāsava
english: "Being beaten with the goad and pricked again and again, he is simply unable to bear that burden. See, O Vāsava!"

sanskrit: tato 'haṃ tasya duḥkhārtā viraumi bhṛśaduḥkhitā aśrūṇy āvartayantī ca netrābhyāṃ karuṇāyatī
english: "Thus I, distressed by his suffering, deeply pained, cry out, shedding tears from my eyes, overcome with compassion."

sanskrit: indra uvāca tava putrasahasreṣu pīḍyamāneṣu śobhane kiṃ kṛpāyitam asty atra putra eko 'tra pīḍyate
english: Indra said: When thousands of your sons are suffering, O beautiful one, why is there compassion only here? Only one son suffers here.

sanskrit: surabhir uvāca yadi putrasahasraṃ me sarvatra samam eva me dīnasya tu sataḥ śakra putrasyābhyadhikā kṛpā
english: Surabhī said: If a thousand sons are mine, they are equally mine in every respect. Yet, O Śakra, for a son who is poor and suffering, my compassion is greater.

sanskrit: vyāsa uvāca tad indraḥ surabhīvākyaṃ niśamya bhṛśavismitaḥ jīvitenāpi kauravya mene 'bhyadhikam ātmajam
english: Vyāsa said: Having heard that speech of Surabhī, Indra was greatly astonished, O Kauravya, and deemed one's own child as even more precious than life itself.

sanskrit: pravavarṣa ca tatraiva sahasā toyam ulbaṇam karṣakasyācaran vighnaṃ bhagavān pākaśāsanaḥ
english: And the Blessed Pākaśāsana poured down copious water right there, creating an obstacle for the ploughman.

sanskrit: tad yathā surabhiḥ prāha samam evāstu te tathā suteṣu rājan sarveṣu dīneṣv abhyadhikā kṛpā
english: As Surabhī said, so let it be with you — let your compassion be greater for all your sons who are afflicted and poor, O king.

sanskrit: yādṛśo me sutaḥ paṇḍus tādṛśo me 'si putraka viduraś ca mahāprājñaḥ snehād etad bravīmy aham
english: As Pāṇḍu is my son, so are you my child, and so is the greatly wise Vidura. I say this out of affection.

sanskrit: cirāya tava putrāṇāṃ śatam ekaś ca pārthiva pāṇḍoḥ pañcaiva lakṣyante te 'pi mandāḥ suduḥkhitāḥ
english: After a long time, your hundred and one sons, O king, are visible, while Pāṇḍu's are only five — and even those five are dull with deep suffering.

sanskrit: kathaṃ jīveyur atyantaṃ kathaṃ vardheyur ity api iti dīneṣu pārtheṣu mano me paritapyate
english: "How shall they live? How shall they prosper?" — thinking thus upon the distressed sons of Pṛthā, my heart burns with anguish.

sanskrit: yadi pārthiva kauravyāñ jīvamānān ihecchasi duryodhanas tava sutaḥ śamaṃ gacchatu pāṇḍavaiḥ
english: If you desire the Kauravas to live here, O Parthiva, let your son Duryodhana make peace with the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca evam etan mahāprājña yathā vadasi no mune ahaṃ caiva vijānāmi sarve ceme narādhipāḥ
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: It is exactly so, O greatly wise sage, as you tell us. I myself know it, and so do all these lords of men.

sanskrit: bhavāṃs tu manyate sādhu yat kurūṇāṃ sukhodayam tad eva viduro 'py āha bhīṣmo droṇaś ca māṃ mune
english: What you consider proper — that which brings prosperity to the Kurus — that very thing Vidura also tells me, and Bhīṣma and Droṇa too, O sage.

sanskrit: yadi tv aham anugrāhyaḥ kauraveṣu dayā yadi anuśādhi durātmānaṃ putraṃ duryodhanaṃ mama
english: If you would do me a favour, if you have compassion for the Kauravas — instruct my evil-souled son Duryodhana.

sanskrit: vyāsa uvāca ayam āyāti vai rājan maitreyo bhagavān ṛṣiḥ anvīya pāṇḍavān bhrātṝn ihaivāsmad didṛkṣayā
english: Vyāsa said: O king, this Blessed Sage Maitreya is coming here, having visited the Pāṇḍava brothers and now wishing to see us here.

sanskrit: eṣa duryodhanaṃ putraṃ tava rājan mahān ṛṣiḥ anuśāstā yathānyāyaṃ śamāyāsya kulasya te
english: This great sage will instruct your son Duryodhana duly and rightly for the peace of your family.

sanskrit: brūyād yad eṣa rājendra tat kāryam aviśaṅkayā akriyāyāṃ hi kāryasya putraṃ te śapsyate ruṣā
english: Whatever this sage says, O lord of kings, that should be done without hesitation. For if the proper act is not done, he will curse your son in anger.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca evam uktvā yayau vyāso maitreyaḥ pratyadṛśyata pūjayā pratijagrāha saputras taṃ narādhipaḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having spoken thus, Vyāsa departed. Then Maitreya appeared, and the lord of men received him with honour together with his sons.

sanskrit: dattvārghyādyāḥ kriyāḥ sarvā viśrāntaṃ munipuṃgavam praśrayeṇābravīd rājā dhṛtarāṣṭro 'mbikāsutaḥ
english: Having offered the arghya and all due rites, when the bull among sages had rested, King Dhṛtarāṣṭra, son of Ambikā, spoke to him with deference.

sanskrit: sukhenāgamanaṃ kaccid bhagavan kurujāṅgale kaccit kuśalino vīrā bhrātaraḥ pañca pāṇḍavāḥ
english: "Did you travel in comfort, O Blessed One, through the Kuru country? Are the five heroic Pāṇḍava brothers in good health?"

sanskrit: samaye sthātum icchanti kaccic ca puruṣarṣabhāḥ kaccit kurūṇāṃ saubhrātram avyucchinnaṃ bhaviṣyati
english: "Do those bulls among men intend to abide by the agreement? Will the brotherhood of the Kurus remain unbroken?"

sanskrit: maitreya uvāca tīrthayātrām anukrāman prāpto 'smi kurujāṅgalam yadṛcchayā dharmarājaṃ dṛṣṭavān kāmyake vane
english: Maitreya said: While proceeding on pilgrimage to sacred fords, I arrived in the Kuru country and by chance saw the Dharmarāja in the Kāmyaka forest.

sanskrit: taṃ jaṭājinasaṃvītaṃ tapovananivāsinam samājagmur mahātmānaṃ draṣṭuṃ munigaṇāḥ prabho
english: Him — clad in matted locks and deer-skin, dwelling in the ascetic forest — groups of sages came to see, that great-souled one, O master.

sanskrit: tatrāśrauṣaṃ mahārāja putrāṇāṃ tava vibhramam anayaṃ dyūtarūpeṇa mahāpāyam upasthitam
english: There I heard, O great king, of the transgression of your sons and the great ruin that has befallen in the form of the dice-game.

sanskrit: tato 'haṃ tvām anuprāptaḥ kauravāṇām avekṣayā sadā hy abhyadhikaḥ snehaḥ prītiś ca tvayi me prabho
english: Then I came to you out of concern for the Kauravas, for my affection and love for you has always been especially great, O master.

sanskrit: naitad aupayikaṃ rājaṃs tvayi bhīṣme ca jīvati yad anyonyena te putrā virudhyante narādhipa
english: This is not fitting, O king, while you and Bhīṣma still live — that your sons should be at strife with one another, O lord of men.

sanskrit: meḍhībhūtaḥ svayaṃ rājan nigrahe pragrahe bhavān kimartham anayaṃ ghoram utpatantam upekṣase
english: You yourself are the central post, O king, for both restraint and support. Why do you ignore this terrible ruin as it rises?

sanskrit: dasyūnām iva yadvṛttaṃ sabhāyāṃ kurunandana tena na bhrājase rājaṃs tāpasānāṃ samāgame
english: By the conduct in the assembly-hall that was like that of bandits, O delight of the Kurus, you do not shine, O king, in the assembly of ascetics.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tato vyāvṛtya rājānaṃ duryodhanam amarṣaṇam uvāca ślakṣṇayā vācā maitreyo bhagavān ṛṣiḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then turning towards King Duryodhana the impatient one, the Blessed Sage Maitreya spoke with gentle words.

sanskrit: duryodhana mahābāho nibodha vadatāṃ vara vacanaṃ me mahāprājña bruvato yad dhitaṃ tava
english: "O Duryodhana of mighty arms, hear my words, O best among speakers, O greatly wise one — what I say that is for your welfare."

sanskrit: mā druhaḥ pāṇḍavān rājan kuruṣva hitam ātmanaḥ pāṇḍavānāṃ kurūṇāṃ ca lokasya ca nararṣabha
english: "Do not act against the Pāṇḍavas, O king; do what is good for yourself, for the Pāṇḍavas, for the Kurus, and for the world, O bull among men."

sanskrit: te hi sarve naravyāghrāḥ śūrā vikrāntayodhinaḥ sarve nāgāyutaprāṇā vajrasaṃhananā dṛḍhāḥ
english: "For they are all tigers among men, heroes who fight with great valour, all with the strength of ten thousand elephants, with bodies firm as the thunderbolt, resolute."

sanskrit: satyavrataparāḥ sarve sarve puruṣamāninaḥ hantāro devaśatrūṇāṃ rakṣasāṃ kāmarūpiṇām hiḍimbabakamukhyānāṃ kirmīrasya ca rakṣasaḥ
english: "All devoted to vows of truth, all honouring themselves as men, slayers of the enemies of the gods, of shape-shifting rakshasas — chief among them Hiḍimba, Baka, and the rakshasa Kirmīra."

sanskrit: itaḥ pracyavatāṃ rātrau yaḥ sa teṣāṃ mahātmanām āvṛtya mārgaṃ raudrātmā tasthau girir ivācalaḥ
english: "That one who, as those great-souled ones were departing from here one night, stood blocking their path, fierce in nature, immovable as a mountain —"

sanskrit: taṃ bhīmaḥ samaraślāghī balena balināṃ varaḥ jaghāna paśumāreṇa vyāghraḥ kṣudramṛgaṃ yathā
english: "— him Bhīma, glorious in battle, best of the strong, slew with the strike used to kill cattle, as a tiger slays a small deer."

sanskrit: paśya digvijaye rājan yathā bhīmena pātitaḥ jarāsaṃdho maheṣvāso nāgāyutabalo yudhi
english: "See, O king, how in the conquest of the directions, Jarāsandha — that mighty archer with the strength of ten thousand elephants — was felled by Bhīma in battle."

sanskrit: saṃbandhī vāsudevaś ca yeṣāṃ śyālaś ca pārṣataḥ kas tān yudhi samāsīta jarāmaraṇavān naraḥ
english: "Vāsudeva is their kinsman by marriage, and Pārṣata is their brother-in-law. What mortal man, subject to old age and death, could stand against them in battle?"

sanskrit: tasya te śama evāstu pāṇḍavair bharatarṣabha kuru me vacanaṃ rājan mā mṛtyuvaśam anvagāḥ
english: "Therefore let there be peace between you and the Pāṇḍavas, O bull of the Bhāratas. Do my bidding, O king; do not fall under the sway of death."

sanskrit: evaṃ tu bruvatas tasya maitreyasya viśāṃ pate ūruṃ gajakarākāraṃ kareṇābhijaghāna saḥ
english: While Maitreya was speaking thus, O lord of men, he — Duryodhana — slapped his own thigh, which was shaped like the trunk of an elephant, with his hand.

sanskrit: duryodhanaḥ smitaṃ kṛtvā caraṇenālikhan mahīm na kiṃ cid uktvā durmedhās tasthau kiṃ cid avāṅmukhaḥ
english: Duryodhana, that dull-witted one, with a smile, scratched the ground with his foot and, saying nothing, stood with his face somewhat averted.

sanskrit: tam aśuśrūṣamāṇaṃ tu vilikhantaṃ vasuṃdharām dṛṣṭvā duryodhanaṃ rājan maitreyaṃ kopa āviśat
english: Seeing Duryodhana inattentive and scratching the earth, O king, anger entered into Maitreya.

sanskrit: sa kopavaśam āpanno maitreyo munisattamaḥ vidhinā saṃprayuktaś ca śāpāyāsya mano dadhe
english: He — Maitreya, that best of sages — having fallen under the power of anger, and being impelled by fate, set his mind upon cursing him.
